body:
Each module can rebuild the same compiler base Option/Result declarations, index maps, names, parameters, cases and fields. Own one paid immutable base-prelude bundle per invocation and lend authenticated overlays/views across module resolution. The existing checked producer schema must remain the sole source of truth; retain all current source/ID authentication and prelude semantics, including shadowing and unused declarations.

Use an invocation owner, never global state or name-use filtering. Current final sequential uncached retention already filters/drops the full prelude, so reduced cumulative construction does not establish reduced peak memory or app recovery. Full synthetic HIR modes still retain rebuilt base payloads.

Own new producer/overlay modules separately from the nominal payload foundation; coordinate shared declaration-index/Resolver/HIR/linker roots through one integrator. Start with a concrete funded lifetime/interface plus complete old constructor controls, and integrate cross-module reuse after the nominal owner foundation.

Discovery: source-only Astra audit at 4ec48420b6e78b1035a66cc406893c46c3028464. This is a real allocation-owner finding, not established application failure causality or measured token/RSS savings. Keep current corrected prelude accounting until a producer-backed replacement is executable. No language caps, work allowances, forecast discounts, global caches, authority shortcuts, or weakened acceptance tests.

Acceptance: complete independently retained original/current HIR, diagnostic, graph/digest, cold/warm cache and backend parity; exact public IDs and order; physical actual allocation/highwater/complete iterative Drop observations; exact/one-short/zero/sticky refusal before acquisition; same cumulative replay work. Original application owners must run unchanged in a later combined batch, with failures disclosed. Publish to wavect/v0-10-0 / PR #761; no per-ticket Cargo jobs.
title: (OPT) Share a paid invocation-owned immutable base prelude across module resolution
